papers.title: Transitive Sets of Mutually Orthogonal Latin Squares
papers.abstract: Write $n=\prod_{i=1}^u p_i^{a_i}$ for the prime factorization of $n$. We prove that a net of order $n$ admitting a point-transitive group of automorphisms preserving each parallel class has at most $\min_i(p_i^{a_i}+1)$ parallel classes. This extends Jungnickel's sharp bound for translation nets. Equivalently, the maximum number of jointly cell-transitive mutually orthogonal Latin squares of order $n$ is $\min_i(p_i^{a_i}-1)$. An explicit Latin square of order nine answers affirmatively Krotov and Potapov's question about the existence of an isotopically transitive, non-topolinear Latin square.

papers.title: A Coarse-Geometric Interpretation of Holt's One-End Theorem
papers.abstract: Can a group be colored red and blue, with both color classes infinite, so that each right translation changes the color of only finitely many elements? For the group of finite subsets of the natural numbers, one can color a nonempty set by the parity of its largest element. Holt proved that no such coloring exists in an uncountable locally finite group. For the finitary coarse structure, almost invariant color classes are exactly the coarsely clopen sets; modulo finite changes, their characteristic functions give all the projections in the Higson corona algebra. We give a detailed account of Holt's coset argument in Cornulier's formulation, without using group cohomology. The argument shows why the space of coarse ends is a singleton and the full Higson corona is connected. We then show, via a separate argument for all slowly oscillating functions, that for any uncountable abelian group---in particular, an uncountable direct sum of groups of order two---Protasov's stronger conclusion holds: the full corona is a singleton.

papers.title: Counting Elements and Conjugacy Classes of Fixed Genus in Hyperbolic Groups
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a non-elementary hyperbolic group equipped with a word metric. A group element in $G$ has orientable genus $n$ if it can be written as the product of $n$ commutators and no fewer. Similarly, a group element in $G$ has non-orientable genus $m$ if it can be written as the product of $m$ squares and no fewer. We obtain the asymptotic order of growth for both the number of group elements and the number of conjugacy classes in $G$, with length at most $L$, and fixed genus (orientable or non-orientable) $n$. For free groups, our methods give precise asymptotics for each of the counts.

papers.title: On the Smallest Cayley Table Fill That Uniquely Determines a Group
papers.abstract: The article investigates the minimal number of cells in a Cayley table that must be filled in order to uniquely determine a group. An exact result is obtained for groups of orders \(2\)--\(23\), and an upper bound is given for an arbitrary order.

papers.title: Nonsolvable critical groups with the spectrum of $S_{10}$
papers.abstract: We classify the nonsolvable finite groups that are critical with respect to the spectrum of the symmetric group $S_{10}$. Up to isomorphism, there are exactly two such groups: $S_{10}$ and $(A_9\times C_3)\rtimes C_2$, where the involution acts on $A_9$ by conjugation by a transposition and on $C_3$ by inversion. The quotient of any nonsolvable group with this spectrum by its solvable radical is almost simple. All possible simple socles are treated without assuming that the radical is nilpotent. The final cases, $L_3(4)$ and $A_6$, are excluded using the canonical subgroup $K=[R(G)\cap G^\infty,G^\infty]$, actions on chief factors, and the required element orders $9,20,30$. In the $A_6$ case, the final contradiction is the existence of an element of order $16$. Reproducible certificates accompany the character-table and matrix calculations.

papers.title: Finite groups with a fixed-point-free automorphism satisfying an irreducible identity
papers.abstract: For any given irreducible polynomial $f(x)=a_0+a_1\cdot x+\cdots+a_d\cdot x^d\in\mathbb{Z}[x]$, we study the structure of finite groups $(G,\cdot)$ that have a fixed-point-free-automorphism $\alpha$ satisfying the condition \[ \{g^{a_0}\cdot\alpha(g)^{a_1}\cdots\alpha^d(g)^{a_d}\mid g\in G\}=\{1\}. \] We show that such a group $G$ is nilpotent of class at most $d^{2^d}$, provided that $|G|$ is coprime to an explicit, non-zero, integer invariant $\iota(f(x))$ of $f(x)$. We do this by extending the solutions of the Frobenius conjecture. We also extend the solution of the restricted Burnside problem in prime exponent and the classification of the $n$-abelian groups.

papers.title: The distortion of finitely generated subgroups in hyperbolic groups
papers.abstract: We show that the range of distortion functions of finitely generated subgroups of hyperbolic groups is essentially as broad as the range of time-complexity functions $T(n)$ of Turing machines. More precisely, we show that for each such $T(n) \geq n$ for which $T(n)^3$ is superadditive, there is a hyperbolic group $G$ with a finitely generated normal subgroup $N$ such that $\text{Dist}_N^G(n) \simeq 2^{T(n)^3}$. Our approach is to estimate the distortion of the kernels in Wise's HNN version of the Rips construction, and then to look at what these estimates yield when the $S$-machine groups of Sapir, Birget, and Rips are the inputs to the construction.

papers.title: Continuous solutions of the complex Kac--Bernstein functional equation on the integers and the real numbers
papers.abstract: In this paper, the continuous solutions of the complex Kac--Bernstein functional equation \[ f_1 ( u + v ) f_2 ( u - v ) f_1 ( u' + v' ) f_2 ( u' - v' ) = f_1 ( u + v' ) f_2 ( u - v' ) f_1 ( u' + v ) f_2 ( u' - v ) \] are classified for $ \mathbb{ Z } $ and $ \mathbb{ R } $. By using this classification for $ \mathbb{ Z } $, we consider a generalization of the Kac--Bernstein theorem on the one-dimensional torus $ \mathbb{ T } $ by Baryshnikov--Eisenberg--Stadje from probability Borel measures to complex Borel measures. Similarly, the original Kac--Bernstein theorem on $ \mathbb{ R } $ is generalized from probability Borel measures to complex Borel measures.

papers.title: Fitting height and lengths of laws in finite solvable groups
papers.abstract: Let G be a finite solvable group, and let h(G) denote its Fitting height, namely the length of a shortest normal series in G with nilpotent factors. We show, that h(G)/5 is a lower bound for the length of any law in G. It follows, that the cardinality of G is bounded from below by an exponential function of h(G). The proof is accomplished by showing an interesting result about the behaviour of non-trivial reduced words in permutation actions of finite solvable groups.

papers.title: Embedding lattices of quasivarieties of periodic groups into lattices of additively idempotent semiring varieties: An algebraic proof
papers.abstract: A general result by Jackson (Flat algebras and the translation of universal Horn logic to equational logic, J. Symb. Log. 73(1) (2008) 90--128) implies that the lattice of all quasivarieties of groups of exponent dividing $n$ embeds into the lattice $L(\mathbf{Sr}_n)$ of all varieties of additively idempotent semirings whose multiplicative semigroups are unions of groups of exponent dividing $n$; the image of this embedding is an interval in $L(\mathbf{Sr}_n)$. We provide a new, direct, and purely algebraic proof of these facts and present a new identity basis for the top variety of the interval. In addition, we obtain new information about the lattice $L(\mathbf{Sr}_n)$, demonstrating that the properties of the lattice for $n\ge 3$ differ drastically from those previously known when $n=1$ or $2$.

papers.title: A marking graph for finite-type Artin groups
papers.abstract: Clean markings on surfaces were a key component in Masur and Minsky's hierarchy machinery, which proved to be a powerful tool in the study of mapping class groups. We construct a marking graph for irreducible finite-type Artin groups which is quasi-isometric to the group modulo its center, i.e., an element of $A_{\Gamma}/Z(A_{\Gamma})$ is determined up to finite error by its action on one of our markings. To construct this graph, we construct suitable collections of transverse parabolic subgroups which extend the maximal simplices of the complex of irreducible parabolic subgroups to analogues of clean markings, and we define natural analogues of elementary moves.

papers.title: Product subcomplexes and intersection complexes of weakly special square complexes
papers.abstract: For compact nonpositively curved square complexes and $\mathrm{CAT}(0)$ square complexes, we define product subcomplexes as equivalence classes of local isometries from products of graphs with embedded coordinate fibers and use them to give a common definition of intersection complexes, reformulating the constructions in the author's earlier paper ``Quasi-isometry invariants of weakly special square complexes'' (Topology and its Applications 307 (2022), 107945). Within this framework, we recover the intended deck quotient description for compact two-sided weakly special square complexes and the quasi-isometry correspondence for their universal covers. Under a simplicity hypothesis on the compact complex, our intersection complex agrees with the image-defined reduced intersection complex in that paper, while finite counterexamples show why images alone do not determine the quotient in general.
